data.content_ref: inline:exp-hist:{"target": "0f5bfba3f8c52d3c79f1a33eb02a21186183c709c54c08d42727d36d1467ebb2", "seq": 1, "objection": "The target's claim that accepting Popper's defense costs the ability to claim preferences track 'verisimilitude' in any formally rigorous sense is factually incorrect regarding Popper's own terms. Popper explicitly developed a qualitative (non-quantitative) definition of verisimilitude in 'Conjectures and Refutations' and later works specifically to maintain that better-corroborated theories can be rationally preferred as closer to the truth, even after the Miller-Tichý refutation of his earlier quantitative attempts. By asserting that the framework forces a retreat to 'purely procedural conventionalism' that cannot guarantee progress toward truth, the target constructs a straw man of Popper's mature position, which retains a realist commitment to truth-likeness as the regulative ideal guiding the preference, distinct from probability but not devoid of truth-content implications.", "outcome": "raised and not answered; the target's status did not move"}
